question: Should Gateway browser-origin allowlisting support scheme-level wildcard entries such as `chrome-extension://*`, and what exact wildcard grammar is acceptable?
rationale: This changes which browser origins can reach Gateway HTTP/WebSocket authorization paths, and current docs intentionally expose only full-origin matches plus the global allow-all wildcard.

options.title: Approve constrained scheme wildcards
options.body: Define a small allowlisted grammar such as hosted opaque schemes only, reject broad regex/hostless patterns, and require source plus handshake coverage before implementation.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Reject scheme wildcards for now and rely on exact opaque-origin fixes plus the existing global `*` escape hatch for intentionally broad local testing.

options.title: Defer to pattern design
options.body: Wait for the loopback `allowedOriginPatterns` work to settle, then decide whether extension scheme wildcards belong in the same contract or a separate one.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained scheme wildcards
recommendation.body: Define a small allowlisted grammar such as hosted opaque schemes only, reject broad regex/hostless patterns, and require source plus handshake coverage before implementation.
